title: Recover immutable event history continuity
objective: Define and prove an explicit trusted-history continuity/reset mechanism for already-laundered immutable control events without silently rewriting published event bytes or allowing a failed transition to become a later trusted baseline.
acceptance: the recovery never silently edits or deletes already-published immutable event files
trusted canonical first-write provenance for the laundered Authority, WorldEntity, and cart events remains externally auditable by exact path and Git blob identity
a failed control transition cannot become a trusted later baseline merely because a descendant commit is validated against its immediate parent
the validator has an explicit reviewed continuity/reset contract for pre-existing corrupted history, with fail-closed semantics outside that finite recovery boundary
state-digest and validation-marker semantics cannot bless untrusted historical mutations
adversarial tests cover failed-transition laundering, descendant-baseline laundering, duplicate/replayed event identities, and recovery-boundary abuse
canonical CI and live control validation are green only after the explicit recovery contract is exercised and independently reviewed
notes: Recovery implementation remains published as PR #420 at exact head 67e89918af03e85863c6eda89fad62a98e314237. Independent reviewer sol-20260812-r420h9k2 returned REQUEST_CHANGES: ADR-0005's stated complete finite reset inventory/source is stale relative to the exact composed foundational + extension manifests and must match the implementation before bootstrap acceptance. Exact-head engine tests/read-only bootstrap candidate remain green; pr-ownership remains intentionally fail-closed until trusted non-bootstrap live state is established.
